text: After a visit, three tools cover almost every money question: pay links, refunds, and returns. And one thing we never do is void a bill that was paid by card.
Here's Tom Chen's billing. He still owes for Biscuit's recheck.
To collect it, click Text pay link.
The text has a secure link for the exact balance.
You'd send it from here. For this demo, click Cancel,
and Don't send.
Email pay link sends the same link for the same balance, so the family can never pay twice. If they ask again, just resend it.
Now a bill Tom already paid by card.
To give money back, click Refund on the payment.
Type the amount. A partial refund is fine,
add the reason,
Leave this box unchecked. Check it only if they'll pay another way, like a different card.
and click Process refund.
It goes back to the same card, through Stripe. The payment now shows the refund. Scout won't let you refund more than the card paid.
And the bill comes down by the same twenty dollars, with a Refund line, so nothing is due.
If the family brought an item back, use Return items instead. It refunds just those items, and the stock goes back on the shelf.
Forgot to charge for something on a paid bill? Don't reopen it or void it. Click New invoice, and add it there.
Voiding is only for lead client liaisons, billing and managers. Here's what a manager sees on this card-paid bill. Click Void invoice,
give a reason,
and click Void.
Scout says no. Voiding would leave the money taken and give the family nothing back. Refund the card first.
Two mistakes to avoid: making a new link every time the family asks, and voiding to give money back. Resend the same link, and refund instead of voiding.
